title: Limits preserve compatible levelwise isomorphisms
statement: Let $\mathcal D$ be a triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Let $(M_n,f_n)$ and $(N_n,g_n)$, indexed by $n\geq1$, be towers whose countable products exist, and choose derived limits $(L,p,\delta)$ and $(L',p',\delta')$ with their Roos triangles [def-weil-derived-limit]. Let $u_n:M_n\to N_n$ satisfy $u_n f_n=g_n u_{n+1}$, and assume every $u_n$ is an isomorphism. For every morphism $\psi:L\to L'$ for which $(\psi,\prod_n u_n,\prod_n u_n)$ is a morphism of the specified Roos triangles (equivalently, $p'\psi=(\prod_n u_n)p$ and $\psi[1]\delta=\delta'(\prod_n u_n)$), $\psi$ is an isomorphism. Thus every Roos-triangle completion denoted by $R\varprojlim u_n$ is an isomorphism; no canonical map or functor is asserted.

proof.text: Compatibility of the tower maps implies that the product map commutes with the transition endomorphisms 1-shift. The specified map ψ and the product map twice therefore form a morphism of the chosen distinguished Roos triangles [def-weil-derived-limit]. The product map is invertible, with inverse the product of the component inverses, as checked on projections. Apply [lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso], equivalently the five lemma for distinguished triangles, to conclude that ψ is an isomorphism. This applies to every completion and does not choose one.

old_proof.text: By the definition of the sequential derived inverse limit, a compatible map of towers acts componentwise on the two product terms and therefore induces a morphism between the corresponding Roos triangles. The component maps are all isomorphisms by hypothesis, so the product map is an isomorphism. Applying the existing levelwise-isomorphism lemma [lem-weil-derived-limit-levelwise-iso] to this morphism of Roos triangles yields that the induced map on derived inverse limits is an isomorphism.
